verses.1:1: Proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel:
verses.1:2: for knowing wisdom and discipline, for discerning sayings of insight;
verses.1:3: for receiving discipline in prudent conduct—righteousness, justice, and equity;
verses.1:4: for giving shrewdness to the naive, to a young man knowledge and discretion.
verses.1:5: Let a wise person listen and increase learning, and let a discerning person acquire guidance,
verses.1:6: to discern a proverb and a figurative saying, words of the wise and their riddles.
verses.1:7: Fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge; fools scorn wisdom and discipline.
verses.1:8: Listen, my son, to your father's discipline, and do not abandon your mother's teaching,
verses.1:9: for they are a wreath of grace for your head and necklaces for your neck.
verses.1:10: My son, if sinners lure you, do not consent.
verses.1:11: If they say, "Come with us; let us lie in ambush for blood, let us lurk for an innocent person without cause;
verses.1:12: let us swallow them alive, like Sheol, and intact, like those descending to the pit.
verses.1:13: We will find all valuable wealth; we will fill our houses with spoils.
verses.1:14: Cast your lot in our midst; there will be one purse for all of us"—
verses.1:15: my son, do not walk along the way with them; restrain your foot from their path,
verses.1:16: for their feet run toward evil, and they rush to shed blood.
verses.1:17: For in vain the net is spread before the eyes of every winged creature,
verses.1:18: yet they lie in ambush for their own blood; they lurk for their own lives.
verses.1:19: Such are the paths of everyone who grasps dishonest gain; it takes the life of its owner.
verses.1:20: Wisdom shouts aloud in the street; in the open squares she lifts up her voice.
verses.1:21: At the head of the bustling streets she calls out; at the entrances of the gates in the city she speaks her sayings:
verses.1:22: "How long, you naive ones, will you love naivety, and scoffers take pleasure in scoffing for themselves, and fools hate knowledge?
verses.1:23: Turn back at my reproof! Look, I will pour out my spirit to you; I will make known my words to you.
verses.1:24: Because I called out and you refused, I extended my hand and no one paid heed,
verses.1:25: and you disregarded all my counsel and did not consent to my reproof,
verses.1:26: I too will laugh at your disaster; I will mock when your terror comes,
verses.1:27: when your terror comes like a tempest and your disaster arrives like a whirlwind, when trouble and anguish come upon you.
verses.1:28: Then they will call to me, yet I will not answer; they will seek me earnestly, yet they will not find me,
verses.1:29: because they hated knowledge, and the fear of the LORD they did not choose;
verses.1:30: they did not consent to my counsel; they treated all my reproof with contempt.
verses.1:31: So they will eat from the fruit of their way, and they will be filled with their own counsels.
verses.1:32: For the turning away of the naive kills them, and the carefree ease of fools destroys them.
verses.1:33: But the one who listens to me will dwell in security, and will be untroubled, free from the terror of harm."
verses.2:1: My son, if you receive my sayings and store up my commandments with you,
verses.2:2: making your ear listen closely to wisdom, inclining your heart toward understanding,
verses.2:3: indeed, if you call for insight and lift up your voice for understanding,
verses.2:4: if you seek her like silver, and like hidden treasures search for her,
verses.2:5: then you will comprehend the fear of the LORD, and you will find knowledge of God.
verses.2:6: For the LORD grants wisdom; out of His mouth come knowledge and understanding.
verses.2:7: For the upright He stores up sound wisdom; He is a shield for those walking in integrity,
verses.2:8: to guard the paths of justice, and He keeps watch over the way of His faithful ones.
verses.2:9: Then you will comprehend righteousness, justice, and equity—every good course.
verses.2:10: When wisdom enters your heart and knowledge is delightful to your soul,
verses.2:11: discretion will keep watch over you; understanding will protect you,
verses.2:12: to rescue you from the way of evil, from a man speaking perverse things,
verses.2:13: those who desert the paths of uprightness to walk in ways of darkness,
verses.2:14: those who are glad to do evil, and exult in the perversities of evil,
verses.2:15: whose paths are twisted, and who are devious in their courses;
verses.2:16: to rescue you from a strange woman, from a foreign woman who makes her sayings smooth,
verses.2:17: who deserts the companion of her youth and has forgotten the covenant of her God;
verses.2:18: for her house sinks down toward death, and her courses toward the departed spirits.
verses.2:19: None who go in to her will return, and they will not reach the paths of life.
verses.2:20: So you may walk in the way of good people, and keep the paths of the righteous.
verses.2:21: For the upright will dwell in the land, and the blameless will stay in it,
verses.2:22: yet the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the treacherous will be torn out of it.
verses.3:1: My son, do not forget my instruction, and let your heart guard my commandments.
verses.3:2: For they will add to you length of days, years of life, and peace.
verses.3:3: Do not let loyal love and faithfulness forsake you; tie them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
verses.3:4: Then you will find favor and good insight in the eyes of God and mankind.
verses.3:5: Trust in the LORD with your whole heart, and do not lean on your understanding.
verses.3:6: In all your ways know Him, and He will straighten your paths.
verses.3:7: Do not be wise in your eyes; fear the LORD and turn aside from evil.
verses.3:8: It will be healing for your navel and refreshment for your bones.
verses.3:9: Honor the LORD from your wealth and from the firstfruits of all your yield.
verses.3:10: Then your storehouses will be filled with abundance, and your vats will burst with new wine.
verses.3:11: My son, do not spurn the LORD's discipline, and do not loathe His reproof.
verses.3:12: For the LORD reproves the one He loves, just as a father does a son in whom he delights.
verses.3:13: Blessed is the person who finds wisdom, and the person who obtains discernment.
verses.3:14: For her gain is better than the gain of silver, and her yield is better than fine gold.
verses.3:15: She is more precious than corals, and none of the things you desire can equal her.
verses.3:16: Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are wealth and honor.
verses.3:17: Her ways are ways of delight, and all her pathways are peace.
verses.3:18: She is a tree of life for those who grasp her, and each one who holds her fast is blessed.
verses.3:19: The LORD by wisdom founded the earth; He established the heavens by discernment.
verses.3:20: By His knowledge the deeps were split open, and the clouds drip dew.
verses.3:21: My son, do not let them depart from your eyes; guard sound wisdom and discretion.
verses.3:22: And they will be life for your soul and grace for your neck.
verses.3:23: Then you will walk in security along your way, and your foot will not trip.
verses.3:24: If you lie down, you will not be frightened; you will lie down, and sweet will be your sleep.
verses.3:25: Do not fear sudden terror, nor the devastation of the wicked when it comes.
verses.3:26: For the LORD will be your confidence, and He will keep your foot from capture.
verses.3:27: Do not withhold good from those entitled to it, when it is in the power of your hand to act.
verses.3:28: Do not say to your neighbor, "Go and return, and tomorrow I will give," when it is with you.
verses.3:29: Do not plot evil against your neighbor while he dwells in security beside you.
verses.3:30: Do not quarrel with a person without cause, if he has dealt you no harm.
verses.3:31: Do not be envious of a man of violence, and choose none of his ways.
verses.3:32: For the crooked person is an abomination to the LORD, but His intimate counsel is with the upright.
verses.3:33: The LORD's curse is in the house of a wicked person, but He blesses the dwelling place of the righteous.
verses.3:34: Though He Himself scoffs at the scoffers, to the humble He gives grace.
verses.3:35: Wise people will inherit honor, but fools lift up disgrace.
verses.4:1: Listen, sons, to a father's discipline, and pay attention to know understanding.
verses.4:2: For I have given you good learning; do not forsake my instruction.
verses.4:3: For I was a son to my father, tender and the only one before my mother.
verses.4:4: And he instructed me and said to me, "May your heart hold fast my words; observe my commandments and live.
verses.4:5: Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding; do not forget, and do not turn aside from the sayings of my mouth.
verses.4:6: Do not forsake her, and she will watch over you; love her, and she will guard you.
verses.4:8: Esteem her highly, and she will exalt you; she will honor you when you embrace her.
verses.4:9: She will set on your head a wreath of grace; a crown of splendor she will bestow on you."
verses.4:10: Listen, my son, and receive my sayings, and years of life will multiply for you.
verses.4:11: In the way of wisdom I have instructed you; I have guided you along courses of uprightness.
verses.4:12: As you walk, your stride will not be cramped, and if you run, you will not stumble.
verses.4:13: Grasp discipline; do not let go; guard her, for she is your life.
verses.4:14: Do not go onto the path of the wicked, and do not stride along the way of evil people.
verses.4:15: Shun it, do not pass along it; swerve away from it and pass on.
verses.4:16: For they do not sleep unless they do evil, and their sleep is snatched away unless they cause someone to stumble.
verses.4:17: For they feed on the bread of wickedness, and they drink the wine of violent deeds.
verses.4:18: Yet the path of the righteous is like radiant light, growing ever brighter until full daylight.
verses.4:19: The way of the wicked is like thick darkness; they do not know what they stumble over.
verses.4:20: My son, pay attention to my words; turn your ear to my sayings.
verses.4:21: Do not let them depart from your eyes; keep them inside your heart.
verses.4:22: For they are life for those who find them, and healing for their entire body.
verses.4:23: Above all that is kept, guard your heart, for from it come the wellsprings of life.
verses.4:24: Remove from yourself crookedness of mouth, and keep deviousness of lips far from yourself.
verses.4:25: Let your eyes look straight ahead, and let your eyelids face directly in front of you.
verses.4:26: Weigh the course of your foot, and all your ways will be firm.
verses.4:27: Do not turn aside to the right or to the left; remove your foot from evil.
verses.5:1: My son, listen attentively to my wisdom; turn your ear to my understanding,
verses.5:2: so that you may guard discretion, and your lips may keep knowledge.
verses.5:3: For the lips of a strange woman drip flowing honey, and her palate is smoother than oil;
verses.5:4: yet her end is as bitter as wormwood, as sharp as a double-edged sword.
verses.5:5: Her feet descend to death; her steps hold fast to Sheol.
verses.5:6: She does not weigh the path of life; her tracks wander, and she does not know it.
verses.5:7: And now, sons, listen to me, and do not turn aside from the words of my mouth.
verses.5:8: Set your way far from her, and do not draw near to the entrance of her house,
verses.5:9: or else you will give your splendor to others and your years to a cruel one,
verses.5:10: or else strangers will have their fill of your strength, and your toils will be in the house of a foreigner,
verses.5:11: and you will groan at your end, when your flesh and your body waste away,
verses.5:12: and you will say, "How I hated discipline, and my heart scorned correction!
verses.5:13: I did not heed the voice of my teachers, and to my instructors I did not turn my ear.
verses.5:14: I was nearly in complete disaster in the middle of the assembly and community."
verses.5:15: Drink water from your own cistern, and flowing waters from within your own well.
verses.5:16: Should your springs disperse outside, streams of water in the open squares?
verses.5:17: May they belong to you alone, and none to strangers with you.
verses.5:18: May your fountain be blessed, and rejoice over the wife of your youth.
verses.5:19: A loving doe and a graceful wild goat—may her breasts satisfy you to the full at all times, and in her love may you be intoxicated continually.
verses.5:20: Why then, my son, should you be intoxicated with a strange woman and embrace the bosom of a foreign woman?
verses.5:21: For the ways of a man lie directly before the eyes of the LORD, and He weighs all his tracks.
verses.5:22: His own iniquities will trap the wicked man, and by the cords of his sin he will be held fast.
verses.5:23: He will die from a lack of discipline, and through the abundance of his folly he will go astray.
verses.6:1: My son, if you have become a guarantor for your neighbor, if you have struck your palms for a stranger,
verses.6:2: you have been ensnared by the words of your mouth; you have been trapped by the words of your mouth.
verses.6:3: Do this then, my son, and free yourself, for you have come into your neighbor's palm: go, humble yourself, and press your neighbor hard.
verses.6:4: Do not grant sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids.
verses.6:5: Free yourself like a gazelle from the hand, and like a bird from the hand of a trapper.
verses.6:6: Go to the ant, sluggard; look at her ways and become wise.
verses.6:7: Though she has no commander, overseer, or ruler,
verses.6:8: she makes ready her bread in the summer and collects her food at the harvest.
verses.6:9: How long, sluggard, will you lie down? When will you get up out of your sleep?
verses.6:10: A bit of sleep, a bit of slumber, a bit of clasping the hands to lie down,
verses.6:11: and your poverty will come like a wanderer, and your scarcity like a shielded warrior.
verses.6:12: A worthless person, a man of iniquity, walks about with a crooked mouth;
verses.6:13: he winks with his eyes, shuffles with his feet, and points with his fingers.
verses.6:14: Perversities are in his heart; he devises evil at all times; he unleashes quarrels.
verses.6:15: Therefore his disaster will come suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered, with no healing.
verses.6:16: These are six things the LORD hates, and seven are an abomination to His soul:
verses.6:17: lofty eyes, a tongue of falsehood, and hands that spill innocent blood,
verses.6:18: a heart devising plans of iniquity, feet hastening to run to evil,
verses.6:19: a witness of falsehood who breathes out lies, and one who unleashes quarrels among brothers.
verses.6:20: Keep, my son, your father's command, and do not abandon your mother's teaching.
verses.6:21: Tie them to your heart continually; bind them around your neck.
verses.6:22: When you walk about, it will guide you; when you lie down, it will keep watch over you; and when you wake up, it will converse with you.
verses.6:23: For a command is a lamp and teaching is a light, and the corrections of discipline are the way of life,
verses.6:24: to guard you from an evil woman, from the smoothness of a foreign woman's tongue.
verses.6:25: Do not covet her beauty in your heart, and do not let her seize you with her eyelids.
verses.6:26: For the cost of a prostitute amounts to a loaf of bread, while a man's wife hunts a precious life.
verses.6:27: Can a man gather fire into his bosom and his garments not be burned?
verses.6:28: Or can a man walk over glowing coals and his feet not be seared?
verses.6:29: Just so is the one who goes in to the wife of his neighbor; no one who touches her will escape punishment.
verses.6:30: People do not look down on a thief if he steals to fill his appetite when he is hungry;
verses.6:31: yet if he is caught, he must repay sevenfold; all the wealth of his house he must give.
verses.6:32: One who commits adultery with a woman is lacking in sense; whoever does it destroys his own life.
verses.6:33: Blows and dishonor he will find, and his shame will not be erased.
verses.6:34: For jealousy is a man's fury, and he will show no compassion on the day of vengeance.
verses.6:35: He will have no regard for any ransom, and he will not consent even if you multiply bribes.
verses.7:1: My son, guard my sayings, and treasure up my commands with you.
verses.7:2: Guard my commands and live, and guard my instruction as the pupil of your eyes.
verses.7:3: Tie them on your fingers; inscribe them on the tablet of your heart.
verses.7:4: Say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and call understanding a close relative,
verses.7:5: to guard you from a strange woman, from a foreign woman who makes her sayings smooth.
verses.7:6: For at the window of my house, through my lattice, I looked down,
verses.7:7: and I saw among the naive, I noticed among the young men, a youth lacking sense,
verses.7:8: passing down the street beside her corner, and striding along the way to her house,
verses.7:9: at twilight, in the evening of the day, in the dead of night and gloom.
verses.7:10: And look, a woman came to meet him, in the attire of a prostitute and secretive of heart.
verses.7:11: She is boisterous and defiant; in her house her feet do not settle.
verses.7:12: Now outside, now in the open squares, and beside every corner she lies in ambush.
verses.7:13: And she took hold of him and kissed him; she made her face brazen and said to him,
verses.7:14: "Sacrifices of peace offerings were due from me; today I have fulfilled my vows.
verses.7:15: Therefore I came out to meet you, to seek your face eagerly; I have found you.
verses.7:16: I have spread my couch with tapestries, colored cloths of linen from Egypt.
verses.7:17: I have scented my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
verses.7:18: Come, let us drink deeply of lovemaking until the morning; let us revel in love.
verses.7:19: For the man is not in his house; he has gone on a journey far away.
verses.7:20: He took the bag of silver in his hand; on the day of the full moon he will come to his house."
verses.7:21: She turned him aside with her abundance of persuasion; with the smoothness of her lips she drove him on.
verses.7:22: At once he goes after her, like an ox that comes to slaughter, and as in shackles to a fool's discipline,
verses.7:23: until an arrow splits his liver, like a bird hurrying to a snare, and he does not know that it is at the cost of his life.
verses.7:24: And now, sons, listen to me, and pay attention to the sayings of my mouth.
verses.7:25: Do not let your heart swerve to her ways; do not wander along her paths.
verses.7:26: For many are the mortally wounded she has brought down, and numerous are all those she has killed.
verses.7:27: Her house is the ways to Sheol, descending to the inner rooms of death.
verses.8:1: Does not wisdom call out, and insight give forth her voice?
verses.8:2: At the top of the heights beside the way, at the junction of the paths she stations herself;
verses.8:3: beside the gates, at the opening of the town, at the entry of the doorways she cries aloud:
verses.8:4: "To you, men, I call out, and my voice is to the sons of mankind.
verses.8:5: Grasp prudence, you naive ones, and you fools, grasp sense.
verses.8:6: Listen, for I speak noble things, and the opening of my lips is uprightness.
verses.8:7: For my palate utters truth, and wickedness is a detestable thing to my lips.
verses.8:8: All the sayings of my mouth are in righteousness; nothing in them is twisted or crooked.
verses.8:9: All of them are plain to the one who understands, and upright to those who find knowledge.
verses.8:10: Take my discipline and not silver, and knowledge rather than select gold.
verses.8:11: For wisdom is better than corals, and all desirable things cannot match her.
verses.8:12: I, wisdom, inhabit prudence, and I find knowledge of discretion.
verses.8:13: The fear of the LORD is hating evil; pride and arrogance, an evil way, and a mouth of perversity I hate.
verses.8:14: Counsel and sound wisdom belong to me; I am understanding; might belongs to me.
verses.8:15: Through me kings reign, and rulers enact justice;
verses.8:16: through me princes govern, and nobles, all righteous judges.
verses.8:17: I myself love those who love me, and those who seek me eagerly will find me.
verses.8:18: Wealth and honor are with me, lasting riches and righteousness.
verses.8:19: My fruit is better than gold, even refined gold, and my produce than select silver.
verses.8:20: On the road of righteousness I walk, in the middle of the paths of justice,
verses.8:21: to cause those who love me to inherit wealth, and I will fill their storehouses.
verses.8:22: The LORD acquired me at the beginning of His way, before His deeds from long ago.
verses.8:23: From eternity I was installed, from the start, from the earliest origins of the earth.
verses.8:24: When there were no deeps, I was brought to birth, when there were no springs heavy with water.
verses.8:25: Before the mountains were sunk in place, before the hills, I was brought to birth,
verses.8:26: while He had not yet made the earth and open fields, or the first of the world's soil.
verses.8:27: When He set up the heavens, there I was; when He traced a circle across the face of the deep,
verses.8:28: when He strengthened the skies above, when the fountains of the deep grew strong,
verses.8:29: when He set the sea its limit, so that the waters would not cross His command, when He traced out the foundations of the earth,
verses.8:30: then I was beside Him, a master artisan, and I was a delight day by day, rejoicing before Him at every moment,
verses.8:31: rejoicing in the world of His earth, and my delight was with the sons of mankind.
verses.8:32: And now, sons, listen to me, and blessed are those who observe my ways.
verses.8:34: Blessed is the person who listens to me, keeping watch at my doors day by day, guarding the doorposts of my entrances.
verses.8:35: For the one who finds me has found life and gains favor from the LORD,
verses.8:36: but the one who misses me does violence to his own life; all who hate me love death."
verses.9:1: Wisdom has built her house; she has carved out her seven pillars.
verses.9:2: She has slaughtered her animals, she has blended her wine; indeed, she has arranged her table.
verses.9:3: She has sent out her servant girls; she calls out from the summits of the heights of the city:
verses.9:4: "Anyone who is naive, let him turn aside here!" As for the one lacking sense, she says to him,
verses.9:5: "Come, dine on my bread, and drink from the wine I have blended.
verses.9:6: Abandon naivety and live, and walk straight in the way of understanding.
verses.9:7: One who corrects a mocker receives dishonor for himself, and one who reproves a wicked person gets himself a blemish.
verses.9:8: Do not reprove a mocker, or he will hate you; reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
verses.9:9: Give teaching to a wise person, and he will become wiser still; instruct a righteous person, and he will add to his learning.
verses.9:10: The start of wisdom is the fear of the LORD, and knowing the Holy One is understanding.
verses.9:11: For through me your days will multiply, and to you years of life will be added.
verses.9:12: If you are wise, it is for yourself that you are wise; and if you mock, you will bear it by yourself."
verses.9:13: The woman of folly is noisy; she is naive and does not know a thing.
verses.9:14: She sits at the entrance of her house, on a seat at the heights of the city,
verses.9:15: to call out to those passing along the way, who keep their paths straight:
verses.9:16: "Anyone who is naive, let him turn aside here!" And as for the one lacking sense, she says to him,
verses.9:17: "Stolen water tastes sweet, and secret bread is delightful."
verses.9:18: Yet he does not know that the departed are there, that in the depths of Sheol are her invited guests.
verses.10:1: The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son is the grief of his mother.
verses.10:2: Treasures of wickedness yield no profit, but righteousness rescues from death.
verses.10:3: The LORD does not leave the soul of a righteous person hungry, but He thrusts aside the craving of the wicked.
verses.10:4: Impoverished is one who works with a slack hand, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
verses.10:5: One who gathers in summer is a discerning son; one who sleeps soundly in harvest is a son who brings disgrace.
verses.10:6: Blessings are upon the head of a righteous person, but the mouth of the wicked hides violence.
verses.10:7: The remembrance of a righteous person is for blessing, but the name of the wicked rots away.
verses.10:8: One wise of heart accepts commands, but one foolish of lips will fall to ruin.
verses.10:9: One who walks in integrity walks in safety, but one who twists his ways will be exposed.
verses.10:10: One who winks the eye causes pain, and one foolish of lips will fall to ruin.
verses.10:11: The mouth of a righteous person is a wellspring of life, but the mouth of the wicked hides violence.
verses.10:12: Hatred rouses quarrels, but love covers over all transgressions.
verses.10:13: On the lips of an understanding person wisdom is found, and for the back of one lacking sense, a rod.
verses.10:14: Wise people treasure up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is ruin close at hand.
verses.10:15: The wealth of a rich person is his strong city; the ruin of the needy is their poverty.
verses.10:16: The earnings of a righteous person lead to life; the income of a wicked person leads to sin.
verses.10:17: One who keeps discipline is a path to life, but one who abandons reproof causes others to stray.
verses.10:18: One who hides hatred has lips of falsehood, and one who brings forth slander is a fool.
verses.10:19: In an abundance of words, transgression does not cease, but one who holds back his lips is discerning.
verses.10:20: Select silver is the tongue of a righteous person; the heart of the wicked is worth very little.
verses.10:21: The lips of a righteous person shepherd many, but through lack of sense fools die.
verses.10:22: It is the blessing of the LORD that brings wealth, and He does not add sorrow with it.
verses.10:23: Carrying out a wicked scheme is like amusement to a fool, and wisdom is the same for a man of understanding.
verses.10:24: The very thing a wicked person dreads will come upon him, but the desire of the righteous will be given to them.
verses.10:25: When a whirlwind sweeps past, a wicked person is no more, but a righteous person is a foundation forever.
verses.10:26: As vinegar is to the teeth and as smoke is to the eyes, so is the lazy person to those who send him.
verses.10:27: The fear of the LORD adds days, but the years of the wicked will grow short.
verses.10:28: The expectation of the righteous is joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
verses.10:29: The way of the LORD is a fortress for the person of integrity, but ruin for doers of iniquity.
verses.10:30: A righteous person will never be moved, but the wicked will not inhabit the land.
verses.10:31: The mouth of a righteous person yields wisdom, but a tongue of perversity will be cut off.
verses.10:32: The lips of a righteous person know what pleases, but the mouth of the wicked knows perversity.
verses.11:1: Deceitful scales are an abomination to the LORD, but a full weight is His pleasure.
verses.11:2: When arrogance comes, disgrace also comes, but wisdom is with the modest.
verses.11:3: The integrity of the upright leads them, but the perversity of the treacherous ruins them.
verses.11:5: The righteousness of a blameless person makes his way straight, but by his wickedness a wicked person falls.
verses.11:6: The righteousness of the upright rescues them, yet the treacherous are trapped by their own craving.
verses.11:7: At the death of a wicked person, hope perishes, and the expectation of strength perishes as well.
verses.11:8: A righteous person is freed from distress, and a wicked person comes in his place.
verses.11:9: By his mouth a godless person ruins his neighbor, but by knowledge the righteous are freed.
verses.11:10: At the well-being of the righteous a city exults, and when the wicked perish there is a jubilant shout.
verses.11:11: Through the blessing of the upright a city rises high, but by the mouth of the wicked it is demolished.
verses.11:12: One who scorns his neighbor is devoid of sense, while a man of discernment stays silent.
verses.11:13: One who goes about with gossip uncovers a secret, but one faithful in spirit keeps a matter concealed.
verses.11:14: Without guidance a people falls, but deliverance is in a multitude of counselors.
verses.11:15: One who acts as guarantor for a stranger will surely come to harm, but one who hates hand-pledges is safe.
verses.11:16: A gracious woman keeps hold of honor, and ruthless men keep hold of wealth.
verses.11:17: A man of kindness benefits his own soul, but a cruel man brings trouble on his own flesh.
verses.11:18: A wicked person earns a false wage, while one who sows righteousness has a genuine reward.
verses.11:19: Steadfast righteousness leads to life, but one who pursues evil goes to his death.
verses.11:20: The twisted in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but those blameless in their way are His pleasure.
verses.11:21: Rest assured, an evil person will not be held guiltless, but the descendants of the righteous will escape.
verses.11:22: Like a ring of gold in a pig's snout, so is a beautiful woman who turns aside from good sense.
verses.11:23: The longing of the righteous is solely good; the hope of the wicked is wrath.
verses.11:24: There is one who scatters and still has more added, and one who holds back more than is right, only to come to want.
verses.11:25: A soul of blessing will be richly supplied, and one who waters others will also be watered himself.
verses.11:26: Whoever keeps back grain, the people curse him, but blessing rests on the head of one who sells it.
verses.11:27: One who eagerly seeks good looks for favor, but as for one who searches after evil, it will come to him.
verses.11:28: One who trusts in his wealth will himself fall, but like a leaf the righteous will flourish.
verses.11:29: One who brings trouble on his household will inherit wind, and a fool is a servant to the wise in heart.
verses.11:30: The fruit of a righteous person is a tree of life, and one who wins souls is wise.
verses.11:31: If indeed a righteous person is recompensed on the earth, how much more a wicked person and a sinner!
verses.12:1: One who loves discipline loves knowledge, but one who hates rebuke is brutish.
verses.12:2: A good person gains favor from the LORD, but He condemns a man of wicked schemes.
verses.12:3: A person will not stand firm through wickedness, but the root of the righteous will never be shaken.
verses.12:4: A worthy wife is her husband's crown, but one who causes shame is like decay in his bones.
verses.12:5: The plans of the righteous are justice; the counsels of the wicked are deceit.
verses.12:6: The words of the wicked are an ambush for blood, yet the mouth of the upright rescues them.
verses.12:7: The wicked are overturned and are gone, yet the household of the righteous stands.
verses.12:8: According to his insight a man is praised, but one of warped heart will be held in contempt.
verses.12:9: Better is one held in low esteem who has a servant than one who exalts himself and lacks bread.
verses.12:10: A righteous person is mindful of the life of his animal, yet the compassion of the wicked is cruel.
verses.12:11: One who cultivates his land will be filled with bread, but one who pursues empty things is devoid of sense.
verses.12:12: A wicked person craves the catch of evildoers, while the root of the righteous produces fruit.
verses.12:13: In the transgression of lips is a snare for an evil person, but a righteous person comes out of distress.
verses.12:14: From the fruit of a man's mouth he will be filled with good, and the recompense of a person's hands will be repaid to him.
verses.12:15: A fool's way is right in his eyes, yet one who listens to counsel is wise.
verses.12:16: A fool's vexation becomes known that very day, yet one who conceals an insult is shrewd.
verses.12:17: One who speaks out truthfully declares what is right, while a witness of lies declares deceit.
verses.12:18: There is one who speaks recklessly like stabs of a sword, while the tongue of the wise gives healing.
verses.12:19: A truthful lip stands firm forever, whereas a tongue of falsehood is only for an instant.
verses.12:20: Deceit is in the heart of those who contrive evil, while for those who counsel peace there is joy.
verses.12:21: No calamity will come upon the righteous, yet the wicked are full of trouble.
verses.12:22: False lips are an abomination to the LORD, yet those who practice faithfulness are His pleasure.
verses.12:23: A shrewd person conceals knowledge, yet the heart of fools announces folly.
verses.12:24: The hand of the diligent will govern, yet slackness will be subjected to forced labor.
verses.12:25: Anxiety in the heart of a man bows it down, while a good word gladdens it.
verses.12:26: A righteous person guides his companion, but the way of the wicked causes them to stray.
verses.12:27: A slack person does not roast his game, but diligence is a person's precious wealth.
verses.12:28: Along the path of righteousness there is life, and on the course of that pathway there is no death.
verses.13:1: A wise son listens to a father's discipline, but a scoffer does not heed rebuke.
verses.13:2: From the fruit of a man's mouth he eats what is good, while the appetite of the treacherous is violence.
verses.13:3: One who guards his mouth keeps his life, but for the one who opens his lips wide there is ruin.
verses.13:4: A sluggard's soul craves, yet there is nothing, while the soul of the diligent will be richly nourished.
verses.13:5: A righteous man hates a word of falsehood, but a wicked man causes a stench and brings disgrace.
verses.13:6: Righteousness guards the one of blameless way, while wickedness overthrows the sinner.
verses.13:7: There is one who acts rich yet has nothing at all, and another who acts poor yet has abundant wealth.
verses.13:8: The ransom for a man's life is his riches, but a poor man does not hear rebuke.
verses.13:9: The light of the righteous is joyful, while the lamp of the wicked dies out.
verses.13:10: Through presumption comes only quarreling, but wisdom is with those who take counsel.
verses.13:11: Wealth from emptiness will dwindle, but one who gathers handful by handful will make it increase.
verses.13:12: Prolonged expectation sickens the heart, but a desire that arrives is a tree of life.
verses.13:13: One who despises a word will be bound in debt to it, but the one who fears a commandment will himself be rewarded.
verses.13:14: The instruction of a wise man is a spring of life, for turning away from the snares of death.
verses.13:15: Good insight yields favor, but the way of the treacherous is rugged.
verses.13:16: Every prudent person acts with knowledge, while a fool spreads out folly.
verses.13:17: A wicked messenger falls into harm, but a faithful emissary brings healing.
verses.13:18: Poverty and disgrace are for the one who disregards discipline, while the one who heeds reproof will be honored.
verses.13:19: A longing realized is pleasant to the soul, but an abomination to fools is turning away from evil.
verses.13:20: One who walks with the wise will grow wise, but one who associates with fools will come to harm.
verses.13:21: Misfortune pursues sinners, but the righteous will be repaid with good.
verses.13:22: A good man bequeaths an inheritance to children's children, while the wealth of a sinner is kept in store for the righteous.
verses.13:23: Much food is in the tilled field of the poor, yet some is swept away for lack of justice.
verses.13:24: One who holds back his rod hates his son, but the one who loves him diligently seeks discipline for him.
verses.13:25: A righteous man eats to the satisfaction of his soul, but the stomach of the wicked goes wanting.
verses.14:1: The wise among women builds her house, but folly demolishes it with her own hands.
verses.14:2: Whoever walks in his uprightness fears the LORD, but the one crooked in his ways despises Him.
verses.14:3: In a fool's mouth is a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise will keep them.
verses.14:4: Without oxen the feeding trough is clean, but abundant harvests come through the strength of an ox.
verses.14:5: A faithful witness will not lie, but a witness of falsehood breathes out lies.
verses.14:6: A scoffer searches for wisdom, yet there is none, while knowledge is easy for the discerning.
verses.14:7: Go away from the presence of a foolish man, for you will not perceive lips of knowledge.
verses.14:8: A prudent person's wisdom is to understand his way, while the folly of fools is deceit.
verses.14:9: Guilt mocks fools, but among the upright there is favor.
verses.14:10: The heart knows the bitterness of its own soul, and an outsider does not share in its joy.
verses.14:11: The house of the wicked will be wiped out, but the tent of the upright will blossom.
verses.14:12: There is a way that looks straight in a man's sight, yet its outcome is the ways of death.
verses.14:13: Even amid laughter a heart can ache, and the outcome of joy is grief.
verses.14:14: One who turns back in heart will be filled from his ways, and a good man will be filled from himself.
verses.14:15: A naive person believes every word, but a prudent person pays close attention to his step.
verses.14:16: A wise man fears and turns away from evil, but a fool is hotheaded and overconfident.
verses.14:17: A short-tempered person commits folly, and a man of schemes will be hated.
verses.14:18: The naive inherit folly, while the prudent crown themselves with knowledge.
verses.14:19: Evil people bow low before good people, and the wicked at the gates of a righteous man.
verses.14:20: Even by his neighbor a poor man is hated, but those who love a rich man are many.
verses.14:21: One who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is the one who shows favor to the humble.
verses.14:22: Do not those who plan evil wander astray? Yet loyal love and truth belong to those who plan good.
verses.14:23: In all toil there will be gain, but talk of the lips leads only to poverty.
verses.14:24: The crown of wise people is their wealth; the folly of fools is folly.
verses.14:25: A truthful witness rescues lives, while one who breathes out lies is deceit.
verses.14:26: In the fear of the LORD there is firm confidence, and for his children there will be a refuge.
verses.14:27: The fear of the LORD is a spring of life, for turning away from the snares of death.
verses.14:28: In an abundance of people is a king's splendor, but in the absence of a populace is a ruler's ruin.
verses.14:29: One who is slow to anger is abundant in understanding, but one who is short of spirit lifts up folly.
verses.14:30: A calm heart is life to the body, but envy is decay to the bones.
verses.14:31: One who oppresses the poor reproaches his Maker, but one who shows favor to the needy honors Him.
verses.14:32: A wicked man is overthrown by his evil, while a righteous man takes refuge in his death.
verses.14:33: In the heart of a discerning person wisdom rests, but in the midst of fools it is made known.
verses.14:34: Righteousness lifts a nation high, but sin is a disgrace to peoples.
verses.14:35: A king's favor is for an insightful servant, while his wrath will be against one who brings shame.
verses.15:1: A gentle reply turns back wrath, but a hurtful word brings up anger.
verses.15:2: The tongue of the wise makes knowledge pleasing, but the mouth of fools pours out folly.
verses.15:3: In every place are the eyes of the LORD, watching over the evil and the good.
verses.15:4: A healing tongue is a tree of life, but perversity in it is a breaking of the spirit.
verses.15:5: A fool spurns his father's discipline, but one who keeps reproof shows prudence.
verses.15:6: In the house of the righteous is abundant wealth, yet in the revenue of the wicked is trouble.
verses.15:7: The lips of the wise scatter knowledge, but the heart of fools is not so.
verses.15:8: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to the LORD, yet the prayer of the upright is His pleasure.
verses.15:9: An abomination to the LORD is the way of the wicked, but the one who pursues righteousness He loves.
verses.15:10: Harsh discipline is for one who abandons the path; the one who hates reproof will die.
verses.15:11: Sheol and Abaddon are before the LORD; how much more the hearts of the sons of mankind!
verses.15:12: A mocker does not love being reproved; to the wise he will not go.
verses.15:13: A joyful heart brightens the face, but by grief of heart the spirit is stricken.
verses.15:14: The heart of a discerning person seeks knowledge, yet the mouth of fools grazes on folly.
verses.15:15: All the days of an afflicted person are bad, yet one with a glad heart has a continual banquet.
verses.15:16: Better is a little in the fear of the LORD than abundant treasure with turmoil in it.
verses.15:17: Better is a meal of vegetables where love is than a fattened ox with hatred in it.
verses.15:18: A wrathful man provokes strife, but one who is slow to anger stills a quarrel.
verses.15:19: The way of a sluggard is like a hedge of briers, but the path of the upright is a built-up highway.
verses.15:20: A wise son gladdens a father, yet a foolish person despises his mother.
verses.15:21: Folly is joy to one lacking sense, but a man of understanding makes his walk straight.
verses.15:22: Plans are thwarted where there is no counsel, but with an abundance of counselors they stand.
verses.15:23: There is joy for a man in the reply of his mouth, and a word in its season—how good it is!
verses.15:24: The path of life goes upward for the insightful, so as to turn aside from Sheol below.
verses.15:25: The LORD pulls down the house of the proud, yet He sets firm the boundary of a widow.
verses.15:26: An abomination to the LORD are plans of evil, but pure are pleasant sayings.
verses.15:27: One who grasps for unjust gain troubles his own house, but one who hates gifts will live. Through loyal love and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and through the fear of the LORD a person turns aside from evil.
verses.15:28: The heart of a righteous person meditates on how to reply, yet the mouth of the wicked pours forth evil things. When the LORD delights in a man's ways, He causes even his enemies to make peace with him.
verses.15:29: Far is the LORD from the wicked, yet the prayer of the righteous He hears. Better is a little in righteousness than abundant revenues without justice. A man's heart devises his way, yet the LORD establishes his step.
verses.15:30: The light of the eyes gladdens the heart; a good report nourishes the bones.
verses.15:32: One who casts off discipline rejects his own soul, but one who listens to reproof acquires sense.
verses.15:33: The fear of the LORD is the discipline of wisdom, and before honor is humility.
verses.16:2: All a man's ways are pure in his own eyes, yet the LORD weighs spirits.
verses.16:5: An abomination to the LORD is everyone lofty in heart; rest assured, he will not be held guiltless.
verses.16:9: The LORD has fashioned everything for its purpose, and even the wicked for the day of calamity.
verses.16:10: An oracle is on a king's lips; in judgment his mouth does not act unfaithfully.
verses.16:11: A balance and scales of justice belong to the LORD; all the weights of the bag are His handiwork.
verses.16:12: An abomination to kings is committing wickedness, for by righteousness a throne is established.
verses.16:13: Righteous lips are the delight of kings, and they love one who speaks what is upright.
verses.16:14: A king's wrath is messengers of death, yet a wise man pacifies it.
verses.16:15: Life is in the light of a king's face, and his favor is like a cloud of spring rain.
verses.16:16: To acquire wisdom—how much better it is than gold! And to acquire understanding is to be chosen over silver.
verses.16:17: The highway of the upright is to turn aside from evil; one who watches over his way guards his soul.
verses.16:18: Before ruin comes pride, and before stumbling comes a lofty spirit.
verses.16:19: Better to be lowly in spirit with the humble than to divide plunder with the proud.
verses.16:20: One who considers a matter wisely will find good, and blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD.
verses.16:21: One who is wise in heart will be called discerning, and sweetness of lips adds persuasiveness.
verses.16:22: A fountain of life is insight to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly.
verses.16:23: The heart of a wise person gives insight to his mouth, and upon his lips it adds persuasiveness.
verses.16:24: Pleasant sayings are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing for the bones.
verses.16:25: There is a way that is right before a man, yet its end is the ways of death.
verses.16:26: A laborer's appetite labors for him, for his mouth presses upon him.
verses.16:27: A worthless man digs up evil, and what is on his lip is like a scorching fire.
verses.16:28: A perverse man sends out strife, and a whisperer separates close companions.
verses.16:29: A violent man lures his neighbor and leads him along a way that is not good.
verses.16:30: One who closes his eyes to devise perverse things, pursing his lips, brings evil to completion.
verses.16:31: Gray hair is a crown of splendor; in the way of righteousness it is found.
verses.16:32: Better is one slow to anger than a mighty warrior, and one who rules over his spirit than one who captures a city.
verses.16:33: Into the lap the lot is cast, yet from the LORD is its whole decision.
verses.17:1: Better is a dry piece of bread and tranquility with it than a house filled with feasts of strife.
verses.17:2: A servant who acts prudently will rule over a son who brings shame, and among brothers he will share an inheritance.
verses.17:3: A crucible is for silver and a smelting furnace is for gold, and the LORD is the examiner of hearts.
verses.17:4: An evildoer pays attention to lips of iniquity; a liar lends an ear to a tongue of destruction.
verses.17:5: One who mocks the poor reproaches his Maker; one who rejoices over disaster will not be held guiltless.
verses.17:6: Children's children are the crown of the elderly, and the splendor of children is their fathers.
verses.17:7: Refined speech is not suitable for a senseless fool; how much less is lying speech for a noble.
verses.17:8: A bribe is a stone of favor in the eyes of its owner; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
verses.17:9: One who covers over a transgression seeks love, but one who repeats a matter divides close companions.
verses.17:10: A rebuke sinks deeper into a discerning person than striking a fool a hundred times.
verses.17:11: An evil person seeks nothing but rebellion, and a cruel messenger will be sent out against him.
verses.17:12: Let a person encounter a bear deprived of her cubs, and not a fool in his folly.
verses.17:13: One who repays evil in return for good—evil will not depart from his house.
verses.17:14: The start of contention is releasing water, so before it erupts, abandon the dispute.
verses.17:15: One who acquits a wicked person and one who condemns a righteous person—both of them are an abomination to the LORD.
verses.17:16: Why is there a purchase price in a fool's hand to acquire wisdom, when he has no good sense?
verses.17:17: At all times a friend shows love, and a brother is born for distress.
verses.17:18: A person lacking sense strikes hands, pledging a guarantee before his neighbor.
verses.17:19: One who loves transgression loves quarreling; one who raises his doorway high seeks ruin.
verses.17:20: One who is crooked in heart will not find good, and one who is twisted in his tongue will fall into harm.
verses.17:21: One who fathers a fool does so to his own grief, and the father of a senseless fool does not rejoice.
verses.17:22: A glad heart promotes healing, but a stricken spirit dries out the bones.
verses.17:23: A wicked person accepts a bribe from the bosom to turn aside the paths of justice.
verses.17:24: Before the face of a discerning person is wisdom, but a fool's eyes are at the ends of the earth.
verses.17:25: A vexation to his father is a foolish son, and bitterness to her who gave him birth.
verses.17:26: Indeed, fining the righteous is not good, nor is striking nobles for uprightness.
verses.17:27: One who holds back his words possesses knowledge; one of a restrained spirit is a person of understanding.
verses.17:28: Even a fool who remains silent is regarded as wise; when he shuts his lips, he is regarded as discerning.
verses.18:1: One who keeps himself apart seeks his own craving; he erupts against all sound judgment.
verses.18:2: A fool has no delight in understanding, only in disclosing his own heart.
verses.18:3: When a wicked person arrives, contempt arrives too, and with dishonor comes reproach.
verses.18:4: Words from a person's mouth are deep waters; the wellspring of wisdom is a gushing stream.
verses.18:5: Showing favoritism to a wicked person is not good, nor is turning aside a righteous person in judgment.
verses.18:6: A fool's lips enter into a dispute, and his mouth calls out for blows.
verses.18:7: The mouth of a fool is destruction to him, and his lips are a trap for his life.
verses.18:8: A whisperer's words are like tasty morsels, and they descend into the inner chambers of the belly.
verses.18:9: Even one who is lax in his work is a brother to a master of destruction.
verses.18:10: A tower of strength is the name of the LORD; into it a righteous person runs and is set safely on high.
verses.18:11: The wealth of a rich person is his fortified city, and like a towering wall in his imagination.
verses.18:12: Before ruin a person's heart grows haughty, and before honor comes humility.
verses.18:13: One who replies before he listens—it is folly and disgrace to him.
verses.18:14: A person's spirit endures his illness, but a stricken spirit—who can bear it?
verses.18:15: The heart of a discerning person acquires knowledge, and the ear of wise people seeks knowledge.
verses.18:16: A person's gift makes space for him and leads him before great people.
verses.18:17: The first one in his lawsuit appears in the right, but his neighbor comes and cross-examines him.
verses.18:18: The lot brings contentions to an end and separates the mighty.
verses.18:19: A wronged brother is more resistant than a fortified city, and contentions are like the bar of a fortress.
verses.18:20: From the fruit of a person's mouth his belly will be filled; with the yield of his lips he will be filled.
verses.18:21: Death and life are in the control of the tongue, and each of those who love it will eat its fruit.
verses.18:22: Whoever finds a wife has found something good and gains favor from the LORD.
verses.19:3: A person's folly overturns his way, yet his heart grows furious against the LORD.
verses.19:4: Wealth adds many companions, but a poor person is separated from his companion.
verses.19:5: A false witness will not be acquitted, and one who breathes out lies will not slip away.
verses.19:6: Many court the favor of a generous person, and everyone is a companion to one who gives gifts.
verses.19:7: All the brothers of a poor person hate him; how much more do his companions stay far from him! He pursues words; they belong to him.
verses.19:8: One who acquires sense loves his soul; one who guards understanding will find good.
verses.19:9: A false witness will not be acquitted, and one who breathes out lies will perish.
verses.19:10: Luxury is not suitable for a fool, much less for a slave to rule over officials.
verses.19:11: A person's insight slows his anger, and his glory is to pass over an offense.
verses.19:12: Like the growling of a young lion is a king's fury, and like dew on grass is his favor.
verses.19:13: A foolish son is a calamity to his father, and a wife's quarrels are a persistent dripping.
verses.19:14: A house and wealth are an inheritance of fathers, yet an insightful wife is from the LORD.
verses.19:15: Laziness causes a deep sleep to fall, and a negligent soul will go hungry.
verses.19:16: One who guards a commandment guards his soul; one who despises his ways will die.
verses.19:17: One who shows favor to a poor person lends to the LORD, and He will pay him back for his deed.
verses.19:18: Discipline your son, since there is hope, and do not set your desire on causing his death.
verses.19:19: A person of great wrath bears the penalty, for if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.
verses.19:20: Listen to counsel and receive discipline, so that you may become wise in your future.
verses.19:21: There are many plans in a person's heart, yet it is the counsel of the LORD that will stand.
verses.19:22: What is desired of a person is his loyal love, and better is a poor person than a liar.
verses.19:23: The fear of the LORD brings life; one spends the night satisfied and will not be visited with harm.
verses.19:24: A sluggard buries his hand in the bowl, and even to his mouth he will not return it.
verses.19:25: Strike a scoffer, and a simple person will grow shrewd; rebuke a discerning person, and he will understand knowledge.
verses.19:26: One who assaults his father and drives off his mother is a son who causes shame and disgrace.
verses.19:27: Stop listening to discipline, my son, and you will wander from the sayings of knowledge.
verses.19:28: A worthless witness scoffs at justice, and the mouth of the wicked swallows iniquity.
verses.19:29: Judgments stand ready for scoffers, and beatings for the back of fools.
verses.20:1: Wine is a scoffer, strong drink is boisterous, and anyone who goes astray by it will not become wise.
verses.20:2: Like the growling of a young lion is the terror of a king; one who provokes him to fury forfeits his life.
verses.20:3: Refraining from strife is an honor for a person, but every fool breaks out in quarreling.
verses.20:4: In autumn a sluggard does not plow, so he begs at harvest, and there is nothing.
verses.20:5: Counsel in a person's heart is deep water, yet a person of understanding will draw it up.
verses.20:6: Many people proclaim, each one, his loyal love, yet who can find a faithful person?
verses.20:7: A righteous person walks in his integrity; blessed are his children after him.
verses.20:8: A king seated on a throne of judgment winnows every evil with his eyes.
verses.20:9: Who can say, "I have purified my heart; I am clean of my sin"? The lamp of one who curses his father and his mother will go out in deep darkness. When an inheritance is gained hastily at first, its outcome will not be blessed. Do not say, "I will pay back evil"; wait for the LORD, and He will rescue you.
verses.20:10: Unequal weights and unequal measures, both of them are an abomination to the LORD.
verses.20:11: Even by his deeds a child makes himself known, whether his work is pure and whether it is upright.
verses.20:12: An ear that hears and an eye that sees, the LORD made both of them.
verses.20:13: Do not love sleep, or you will be impoverished; open your eyes, and you will have your fill of bread.
verses.20:23: An abomination to the LORD are unequal weights, and deceitful scales are not good.
verses.20:24: From the LORD are a man's steps; so how can a person understand his way?
verses.20:25: It is a snare for a person to blurt out, "It is sacred," and to reflect after vows.
verses.20:26: A wise king winnows the wicked and brings a wheel back over them.
verses.20:27: The lamp of the LORD is a person's spirit, searching all the chambers of the inner being.
verses.20:28: Loyal love and faithfulness guard a king, and by loyal love he upholds his throne.
verses.20:29: Young men's glory is their strength, and old men's splendor is gray hair.
verses.20:30: Wounding bruises are a scouring away of evil, and blows scour the chambers of the inner being.
verses.21:1: A king's heart is like streams of water in the hand of the LORD; He turns it toward whatever He desires.
verses.21:2: Every way of a man is straight in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs hearts.
verses.21:3: Doing righteousness and justice is preferred by the LORD over sacrifice.
verses.21:4: Lofty eyes and an arrogant heart—the lamp of the wicked—are sin.
verses.21:6: Gaining treasures by a lying tongue is a driven vapor for those who seek death.
verses.21:7: The violence of the wicked will drag them off, because they refuse to do justice.
verses.21:8: Twisted is the way of a guilty man, but as for the pure, his action is straight.
verses.21:9: It is better to live on a corner of a roof than with a contentious wife in a shared house.
verses.21:10: The soul of a wicked man craves evil; his neighbor is shown no favor in his eyes.
verses.21:11: When a scoffer is punished, the simple grows wise, and when insight is given to a wise man, he receives knowledge.
verses.21:12: The Righteous One examines the house of a wicked man, overturning the wicked to ruin.
verses.21:13: One who stops up his ear against the outcry of the poor—he too will call out and will not be answered.
verses.21:14: A gift in secret quells anger, and a bribe in the bosom, fierce wrath.
verses.21:15: To do justice is a joy to the righteous, yet terror to workers of iniquity.
verses.21:16: A person who strays from the way of insight will rest in the gathering of the dead.
verses.21:17: One who loves pleasure will be a man of want; one who loves wine and oil will not grow rich.
verses.21:18: A ransom for the righteous is a wicked man, and in place of the upright is a treacherous one.
verses.21:19: It is better to live in a wilderness land than with a contentious and irritable wife.
verses.21:20: Desirable treasure and oil are in the dwelling of a wise person, yet a foolish person swallows it up.
verses.21:21: One who pursues righteousness and steadfast love finds life, righteousness, and honor.
verses.21:22: A wise man scales a city of warriors and pulls down the stronghold of its confidence.
verses.21:23: One who guards his mouth and his tongue guards his soul from distresses.
verses.21:24: An insolent, arrogant man—"Scoffer" is his name—acts with the fury of insolence.
verses.21:25: The craving of a sluggard kills him, because his hands refuse to work.
verses.21:26: All day long he greedily craves, yet a righteous man gives and does not withhold.
verses.21:27: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination, all the more when he brings it with a wicked purpose.
verses.21:28: A lying witness will perish, but a man who listens will speak forever.
verses.21:29: A wicked man hardens his face, but as for the upright, he considers his way.
verses.21:30: There is no wisdom, there is no understanding, and there is no counsel against the LORD.
verses.21:31: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, yet to the LORD belongs the victory.
verses.22:1: A reputation is to be chosen over abundant wealth; better than silver and gold is favor.
verses.22:2: Rich and poor meet each other; the Maker of them all is the LORD.
verses.22:3: A shrewd person sees calamity and hides himself, while the simple continue on and are punished.
verses.22:4: The reward of humility—the fear of the LORD—is wealth and honor and life.
verses.22:5: Thorns and traps are on the way of a perverse man; one who guards his soul will stay far away from them.
verses.22:7: A rich man rules over the poor, and a borrower is a slave to the man who lends.
verses.22:8: One who sows injustice will reap trouble, and the rod of his fury will come to an end.
verses.22:9: One with a generous eye will himself be blessed, because he gives from his bread to the poor.
verses.22:10: Drive out a scoffer, and contention will leave, and dispute and disgrace will cease.
verses.22:11: One who loves purity of heart, whose lips are gracious—a king is his friend.
verses.22:12: The eyes of the LORD guard knowledge, but He overturns the words of a treacherous man.
verses.22:13: A sluggard says, "There is a lion outside! In the middle of the public squares I will be murdered!"
verses.22:14: A deep pit is the mouth of forbidden women; one denounced by the LORD will fall into it.
verses.22:15: Foolishness is fastened in the heart of a youth; a rod of discipline will put it far away from him.
verses.22:16: One who oppresses the poor to gain more for himself, and one who gives to a rich man, will come only to want.
verses.22:17: Turn your ear and listen to the words of the wise, and set your heart on my knowledge.
verses.22:18: For it is pleasant when you guard them within you; they will be ready together on your lips.
verses.22:19: So that your confidence may be in the LORD, I have informed you today—even you.
verses.22:20: Have I not written for you noble things with counsels and knowledge,
verses.22:21: to make known to you the reliability of sayings of truth, so that you may bring back true sayings to those who sent you?
verses.22:22: Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush an afflicted man in the gate.
verses.22:23: For the LORD will argue their case, and He will despoil of life those who despoil them.
verses.22:24: Do not befriend a man prone to anger, and do not go with a furious man,
verses.22:25: or else you will learn his paths and take a snare for your soul.
verses.22:26: Do not be among those who strike hands, among those who guarantee debts.
verses.22:27: If you have nothing to pay with, why should he take your bed from beneath you?
verses.22:28: Do not displace an ancient boundary that your fathers established.
verses.22:29: Have you seen a man proficient in his work? Before kings he will take his stand; he will not take his stand before obscure men.
verses.23:1: When you sit to eat with a ruler, take careful note of what is before you,
verses.23:2: and set a knife to your throat if you have a strong appetite.
verses.23:3: Do not crave his delicacies, for it is bread of deception.
verses.23:4: Do not toil to become rich; cease from your own understanding.
verses.23:5: Will you cast your eyes upon it, and it is gone? For it surely makes wings for itself; like an eagle it flies into the sky.
verses.23:6: Do not eat the bread of one with a grudging eye, and do not crave his delicacies.
verses.23:7: For just as he reckons within himself, so is he. "Eat and drink," he tells you, yet his heart is not with you.
verses.23:8: The morsel you ate you will vomit up, and you will ruin your pleasant words.
verses.23:9: Do not speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the insight of your words.
verses.23:10: Do not shift an ancient boundary, and do not enter the fields of orphans,
verses.23:11: for their Redeemer is mighty; He Himself will argue their case against you.
verses.23:12: Bring your heart to discipline, and your ear to sayings of knowledge.
verses.23:13: Do not withhold discipline from a youth; if you strike him with the rod, he will not die.
verses.23:14: Strike him with the rod yourself, and you will rescue his soul from Sheol.
verses.23:15: My son, if your heart grows wise, my own heart will rejoice as well,
verses.23:16: and my inner being will exult when your lips speak uprightness.
verses.23:17: Do not let your heart envy sinners; rather, be zealous in the fear of the LORD all day long.
verses.23:18: For indeed there is a future, and your expectation will not be cut off.
verses.23:19: You, my son, listen and grow wise, and guide your heart in the way.
verses.23:20: Do not be among heavy wine drinkers, among those who gorge themselves on meat,
verses.23:21: for a heavy drinker and a glutton will become impoverished, and drowsiness will dress them in rags.
verses.23:22: Listen to your father who fathered you, and when your mother has grown old, do not despise her.
verses.23:24: The father of a righteous one will surely exult, and the one who fathers a wise one will be glad in him.
verses.23:25: May your father and your mother be glad, and may she who gave birth to you exult.
verses.23:26: Give your heart to me, my son, and let your eyes watch my ways.
verses.23:27: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and a foreign woman is a narrow well.
verses.23:28: Moreover, she lies in ambush like a bandit, and multiplies the treacherous among mankind.
verses.23:29: Who has woe? Who has misery? Who has quarrels? Who has lamenting? Who has wounds for no reason? Who has bloodshot eyes?
verses.23:30: Those who stay late over wine, those who go to search out mixed wine.
verses.23:31: Do not gaze at wine when it turns red, when it gives its gleam in the cup, when it glides smoothly.
verses.23:32: At the end, like a serpent it bites, and like a viper it stings.
verses.23:33: Your eyes will see strange sights, and your heart will speak twisted things.
verses.23:34: And you will be like one lying down in the heart of the sea, and like one lying atop a mast.
verses.23:35: "They struck me, yet I felt no pain; they pounded me, yet I did not know it. When will I wake up? I will seek it once again."
verses.24:1: Do not envy men of evil, and do not crave to be with them,
verses.24:2: for their heart plots violence, and their lips speak trouble.
verses.24:3: Through wisdom a house is built, and through discernment it is firmly established;
verses.24:4: and through knowledge rooms are filled with all precious and pleasant wealth.
verses.24:5: A wise man has strength, and a man of knowledge intensifies power.
verses.24:6: For by skillful guidance you will wage your war, and victory is in a multitude of counselors.
verses.24:7: Wisdom is too lofty for a fool; at the gate he does not open his mouth.
verses.24:8: Whoever plots to do evil, people will call him a master of schemes.
verses.24:9: The scheming of folly is sin, and a mocker is an abomination to mankind.
verses.24:10: If you falter in a day of distress, your strength is meager.
verses.24:11: Rescue those being taken to death, and surely hold back those tottering to slaughter.
verses.24:12: If you say, "Look, we did not know this," does not the One who weighs hearts discern it? Does not the One who guards your soul know it? And will He not repay a person according to his deed?
verses.24:13: Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and honeycomb is sweet to your palate.
verses.24:14: Know that wisdom is just like that for your soul; if you find it, then there is a future, and your expectation will not be cut off.
verses.24:15: Do not lie in ambush, wicked man, against the dwelling of a righteous person; do not ravage his resting place,
verses.24:16: for seven times a righteous person falls and rises, but the wicked stumble in disaster.
verses.24:17: When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and when he stumbles, do not let your heart exult,
verses.24:18: otherwise the LORD will see it and it will be evil in His eyes, and He will turn His anger away from him.
verses.24:19: Do not fret over evildoers; do not envy the wicked,
verses.24:20: for there will be no future for the evil person; the lamp of the wicked will go out.
verses.24:21: Fear the LORD, my son, and the king; do not mingle with those prone to change,
verses.24:22: for suddenly their disaster will arise, and who knows the ruin from the two of them?
verses.24:23: These also belong to the wise: Showing partiality in judgment is not good.
verses.24:24: One who says to a wicked person, "You are righteous"—peoples will curse him, nations will denounce him;
verses.24:25: but it will go well for those who rebuke, and upon them a blessing of good will come.
verses.24:26: One who gives a straightforward reply kisses the lips.
verses.24:27: Prepare your work outdoors, and get it ready for yourself in the field; afterward, build your house.
verses.24:28: Do not be a witness without cause against your neighbor. And would you deceive with your lips?
verses.24:29: Do not say, "Just as he did to me, so I will do to him; I will repay the man according to his deed."
verses.24:30: I went past the field of a lazy man, and past the vineyard of a person lacking understanding,
verses.24:31: and look, all of it had grown up with thistles, its surface was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was torn down.
verses.24:32: Then I myself gazed at it and set my heart to it; I saw it, and I took instruction:
verses.24:33: A little sleep, a little dozing, a little folding of the hands to lie down—
verses.24:34: and your poverty will come prowling, and your needs like an armed warrior.
verses.25:1: These too are proverbs of Solomon that the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah, transcribed.
verses.25:2: The glory of God is concealing a matter, and the glory of kings is searching out a matter.
verses.25:3: The heavens for height and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings—there is no searching it out.
verses.25:4: Remove dross from silver, and a vessel comes out for the refiner.
verses.25:5: Remove a wicked person from before a king, and his throne will stand firm in righteousness.
verses.25:6: Do not exalt yourself before a king, and in the place of the great do not stand.
verses.25:7: For it is better to be told, "Come up here," than to be brought low before a noble whom your eyes have seen.
verses.25:8: Do not go out hastily to dispute; otherwise, what will you do at its end when your neighbor shames you?
verses.25:9: Plead your dispute with your neighbor, and do not disclose the secret of another,
verses.25:10: or one who hears will disgrace you, and your bad reputation will not turn back.
verses.25:11: Golden apples in silver settings—a word spoken at its proper moment.
verses.25:12: A gold earring and a jewel of pure gold—a wise reprover to an ear that listens.
verses.25:13: Like the coolness of snow on a day of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him, and he restores the soul of his masters.
verses.25:14: Clouds and wind, and no rain—a man who boasts of a false gift.
verses.25:15: By patience a ruler is persuaded, and a gentle tongue breaks a bone.
verses.25:16: If you find honey, eat what is sufficient for you, or you will get your fill of it and vomit it up.
verses.25:17: Keep your foot scarce in your neighbor's house, or he will get his fill of you and hate you.
verses.25:18: A war club and a sword and a sharpened arrow—a man who testifies against his neighbor as a false witness.
verses.25:19: A broken tooth and a faltering foot—reliance on a treacherous person on a day of distress.
verses.25:20: One who removes a garment on a day of cold, vinegar on alkali—so is one who sings songs to a sorrowful heart.
verses.25:21: If the one who hates you is hungry, feed him bread, and if he is thirsty, give him a drink of water,
verses.25:22: for you will pile glowing coals onto his head, and the LORD will repay you.
verses.25:23: A north wind produces rain, and a secret tongue, an indignant face.
verses.25:24: It is better to dwell on a corner of a roof than with a quarrelsome wife in a shared house.
verses.25:25: Cold water upon an exhausted soul—so is a good report from a faraway land.
verses.25:26: A fouled spring and a ruined fountain—a righteous person wavering before the wicked.
verses.25:27: Eating honey in excess is not good, and searching out one's own glory is no glory.
verses.25:28: A breached city without a wall—a man who has no restraint over his spirit.
verses.26:1: Like snow during summer and like rain during harvest, so honor is not suitable for a fool.
verses.26:2: Like a bird in wandering, like a swallow in flying, so a curse without cause comes to him.
verses.26:3: A whip for a horse, a bit for a donkey, and a rod for the back of fools.
verses.26:4: Do not reply to a fool in keeping with his folly, otherwise you too will become like him.
verses.26:5: Reply to a fool in keeping with his folly, otherwise he will become wise in his own eyes.
verses.26:6: Cutting off his own feet, drinking violence—so is one who sends messages by a fool's hand.
verses.26:7: Legs hang limp from a lame person—and so too a proverb in the mouth of fools.
verses.26:8: Like binding a stone into a sling, so is the one who gives a fool honor.
verses.26:9: A thorn goes up into a drunkard's hand—and so too a proverb in the mouth of fools.
verses.26:10: An archer piercing everyone—so is one who hires a fool, and one who hires passersby.
verses.26:11: As a dog turns back to its vomit, a fool repeats himself in his folly.
verses.26:12: Have you seen a man wise in his own eyes? A fool has more hope than he does.
verses.26:13: A sluggard says, "A lion is on the road, a lion among the public squares!"
verses.26:14: The door turns on its hinge, and a sluggard on his bed.
verses.26:15: A sluggard buries his hand in the bowl; he grows too weary to return it to his mouth.
verses.26:16: In his own eyes a sluggard is wiser than seven who answer with discernment.
verses.26:17: One who seizes the ears of a dog—so is a passerby who gets worked up over a dispute not his own.
verses.26:18: Like a crazed person who shoots firebrands, arrows, and death,
verses.26:19: so is a man who has deceived his neighbor and says, "Am I not joking?"
verses.26:20: Where wood is lacking, a fire dies out, and where there is no gossiper, strife subsides.
verses.26:21: Charcoal for glowing coals and wood for fire—so is a quarrelsome man for kindling a dispute.
verses.26:22: The words of a gossiper are like savory morsels, and they descend into the inner chambers of the belly.
verses.26:23: Silver dross plated over earthenware—ardent lips and an evil heart.
verses.26:24: With his lips the one who hates disguises himself, while within himself he stores up deceit.
verses.26:25: When he makes his voice gracious, do not trust in him, for seven abominations are in his heart.
verses.26:26: Though hatred conceals itself in deception, his evil will be uncovered in the assembly.
verses.26:27: One who digs a pit falls into it, and one who rolls a stone—it turns back upon him.
verses.26:28: A false tongue hates those crushed by it, and a smooth mouth produces downfall.
verses.27:1: Do not boast in the day of tomorrow, because you do not know what a day will give birth to.
verses.27:2: Let a stranger praise you, and not your mouth; a foreigner, and not your lips.
verses.27:3: Heavy is a stone and weighty is sand, yet the vexation of a fool is heavier than both of them.
verses.27:4: Fury is cruel, and anger is a torrent, yet who can stand in the face of jealousy?
verses.27:5: Open reproof is better than concealed love.
verses.27:6: Trustworthy are the wounds of one who loves, but profuse are the kisses of one who hates.
verses.27:7: A satisfied soul tramples on honeycomb, yet to a hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
verses.27:8: Like a bird wandering from its nest, so is a man wandering from his place.
verses.27:9: Oil and incense gladden a heart, and the sweetness of one's friend comes from heartfelt counsel.
verses.27:10: Do not abandon your friend and your father's friend, and do not enter your brother's house on the day of your disaster; a nearby neighbor is better than a distant brother.
verses.27:11: Be wise, my son, and gladden my heart, so that I may return an answer to the one who taunts me.
verses.27:12: A shrewd person sees trouble and hides himself, while the naive pass on and suffer punishment.
verses.27:13: Take his garment, because he has stood as security for a stranger; and on behalf of a foreign woman, take a pledge from him.
verses.27:14: One who blesses his friend in a loud voice early in the morning—it will be counted as a curse to him.
verses.27:15: A persistent dripping on a day of pouring rain and a quarrelsome wife are alike.
verses.27:16: Whoever holds her back holds back the wind, and his right hand encounters oil.
verses.27:17: Iron is sharpened by iron, and a man sharpens the face of his friend.
verses.27:18: One who tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and one who watches over his master will be honored.
verses.27:19: As in water face corresponds to face, so does a person's heart to a person.
verses.27:20: Sheol and Abaddon are not satisfied, and the eyes of a person are not satisfied.
verses.27:21: A crucible is for silver and a furnace is for gold, and a man is measured by his praise.
verses.27:22: Even if you pound the fool in a mortar among crushed grain with a pestle, his folly will not leave him.
verses.27:23: Know thoroughly the condition of your flock; set your heart on the herds.
verses.27:24: For wealth is not forever, and does a crown last from generation to generation?
verses.27:25: The grass vanishes, fresh shoots appear, and the vegetation of the mountains is gathered.
verses.27:26: Lambs are for your clothing, and male goats are the price of a field.
verses.27:27: And there is enough goat milk for your food, for your household's food, and sustenance for your female servants.
verses.28:1: The wicked flee with no one pursuing, but the righteous are confident like a young lion.
verses.28:2: By the transgression of a land its rulers are many, yet by a discerning and knowledgeable person, right order lasts long.
verses.28:3: A poor man who oppresses the needy is a sweeping rain that leaves no bread.
verses.28:4: Those who abandon the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law contend against them.
verses.28:5: Men of evil do not understand justice, yet those who seek the LORD understand everything.
verses.28:6: A poor person who walks in his integrity is better than one who is crooked in his ways, though he is rich.
verses.28:7: One who guards the law is a discerning son, but one who associates with gluttons brings shame on his father.
verses.28:8: One who multiplies his wealth through interest and usury amasses it for the one who shows favor to the needy.
verses.28:9: One who turns his ear away from hearing the law—even his prayer is a detestable thing.
verses.28:10: One who misleads the upright onto an evil path—he himself will fall into his own pit, while the blameless will inherit what is good.
verses.28:11: Wise in his own eyes is a rich man, but a needy person who has discernment searches him out.
verses.28:12: When the righteous exult, there is great splendor, yet when the wicked rise, people must be searched for.
verses.28:13: One who covers his transgressions will not succeed, but one who confesses and abandons them will be shown mercy.
verses.28:14: Blessed is the person who fears continually, but one who hardens his heart will fall into trouble.
verses.28:15: A roaring lion and a prowling bear—that is a wicked ruler over a needy people.
verses.28:16: A leader who lacks understanding abounds in acts of oppression, while one who hates dishonest gain will lengthen his days.
verses.28:17: A person weighed down by the blood of a life will flee to the pit; let no one lend him support.
verses.28:18: One who walks blamelessly will be saved, yet one who is crooked in his ways will fall at once.
verses.28:19: One who tills his ground will get his fill of bread, but one who chases empty things will get his fill of poverty.
verses.28:20: A trustworthy man abounds in blessings, but one who rushes to get rich will not be held guiltless.
verses.28:21: Showing partiality is not good, yet for a morsel of bread a man will transgress.
verses.28:22: A stingy man is frantic for wealth, and he does not know that lack will come upon him.
